ops.title: RESOLVED structurally by Holder v2 (fusekit v1.0.0, fleet migrated 2026-07-12): journal v2 is identity-only — no policy fields exist to skew. Keep for the general rule: any journaled per-mount policy + independently-upgradeable holder cask = skew hazard

ops.body:
Found 2026-07-10 by the whole-P1 review (I had wrongly reasoned this unreachable; the review corrected me).

**The insight (durable, generalizes to any journaled per-mount field).** The self-owning holder's spec journal + the fact that the holder CASK is independently upgradeable from the consumer LIBRARY creates a policy-skew hazard: a consumer linking a PRE-journal fusekit (cc-pool v0.50.x on fusekit v0.36, sends no `carcass_policy`) mounts through the SHARED cask holder at `mountd.DefaultHolderSocket` (accepted because `MinHolderVersion` is only v0.29.0). If that holder is an independently-upgraded v0.38+ cask, it journals the policy-LESS Mount with `CarcassPolicy=""` — which `forcedRoots` (fusekit journal.go) treats as **force**. Upgrading the consumer to the defer-setting v0.51 does NOT repair the row: the idempotent OpMount path returns OK BEFORE any journal write (fusekit mountd/server.go:526), and healthy live rows are never re-Mounted. So on a later holder crash, replay `ClearCarcass` can `MNT_FORCE` a wedged-but-session-live mux root → the `nfs_vinvalbuf2` Apple-NFS-kext panic class ([[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]]).

Note: the P1 delta's OWN policy propagation is CORRECT (defer reaches every MountSpec incl. the mux root, pinned by TestOverlaySpecDefersCarcassOnMuxRoot). The hazard is purely the deployment-skew journal window — a lifecycle gap, not a propagation bug.

**Fix (rides cc-pool v0.51.0):**
- fusekit v0.38.5: idempotent OpMount REFRESHES the journaled CarcassPolicy/IdlePolicy from the request before returning OK (so a re-issued Mount updates force→defer). (Ship alongside claim-serialized RevokeIdle — the R2-4 revoke-vs-sweep fence.) Do NOT broadly flip replay's absent→defer default — that would wrongly override consumers like cc-notes that intentionally set force.
- cc-pool: at daemon startup, re-issue Mount (or a policy-refresh) for every healthy fuse row so the holder's row gets the defer/attest policy; bump `MinHolderVersion` past the fixed holder so the defer+attest contract is actually guaranteed by the holder cc-pool hosts on.

**General rule:** whenever a consumer relies on a per-mount policy the holder journals, a mixed-version window can strand a policy-less/old-default row that the consumer upgrade won't rewrite — the holder must refresh journaled policy on idempotent re-mount, and consumers must re-assert policy + gate on a `MinHolderVersion` that guarantees it. Related: [[creds-fresher-wins-decision]] (the analogous "later value wins" resolution for creds).
